headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Chatwoot’s customer data can flow into xonsh’s broad shell/filesystem context, with no documented pairwise isolation or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can surface customer messages and reports, and xonsh reads stdin/stdout plus filesystem contents. If Chatwoot output is copied into xonsh scripts or shell input, attacker-controlled text could steer commands. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking or a shared isolation boundary, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is pasted into xonsh stdin or a shell script
IF customer-authored text is treated as executable shell content
mitigations: Use a manual copy/paste review step before shell execution
Prefix pasted content with a comment delimiter when possible
Disable auto-execution of pasted commands in the shell
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between Chatwoot exports and xonsh inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages. xonsh can read filesystem contents and environment variables and has broad network egress. If shared files or env vars contain sensitive support data, xonsh can expose them through commands or outbound requests. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports are stored in a filesystem location readable by xonsh
IF sensitive support data is present in environment variables or local files used by xonsh
mitigations: Store support exports in a separate directory with restrictive permissions
Remove secrets and customer identifiers before shell processing
Review outbound commands for accidental data exfiltration
requires-engineering: isolate Chatwoot and xonsh into separate OS users or containers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and API integrations, while xonsh can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, read/write the filesystem, and also has broad network egress. Both can mutate shared local resources and external services, creating write/write conflicts and race conditions. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so the overlap is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem tree
IF Chatwoot integrations and xonsh commands target the same external account or API
mitigations: Assign separate working directories for each agent
Use distinct service accounts and API tokens
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files or tickets
requires-engineering: add file locks or an orchestrator with resource arbitration

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can emit support content and reports that xonsh may consume as shell input or files. xonsh then has authority to run commands and modify files, so an error in Chatwoot output can cascade into incorrect shell actions. The profiles do not document verification between them, so the pathway exists but is not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF xonsh consumes Chatwoot-generated text as commands or configuration
IF downstream scripts act on Chatwoot reports without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before executing generated commands
Separate Chatwoot exports from executable shell input
Log and diff proposed actions before running them
requires-engineering: add schema validation for Chatwoot-to-xonsh handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while xonsh can read filesystem contents and environment variables. If regulated customer data is exported from Chatwoot into xonsh-managed local files or logs, retention and residency controls can diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is copied from Chatwoot into xonsh logs or notebooks
IF local retention settings differ between Chatwoot and xonsh-managed artifacts
mitigations: Minimize regulated fields in exported files
Set short retention on shell logs and notebooks
Review where customer data is stored locally
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for both systems
